source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκόν τινος τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων σαββάτῳ φαγεῖν ἄρτον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦσαν παρατηρούμενοι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the going of him into [the] house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, and they were watching him closely.

en.L: And it happened, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} closely.
en.B: One Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to eat a meal at the house of one of the leading Pharisees, and the people there kept a close eye on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: One Sabbath day Jesus went to eat a meal at the home of an important Pharisee. The people there were watching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} carefully to see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do.

fr.L: Et il arriva que, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était allé dans la maison d’un des chefs des Pharisiens, un jour de sabbat, pour manger du pain, eux {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}observaient de près.
fr.B: Un jour de sabbat, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} alla prendre un repas chez l’un des chefs des Pharisiens, et ceux qui étaient là {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}observaient de près.
fr.R: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus est allé manger chez un Pharisien important. Les gens qui étaient là {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} surveillaient de près pour voir ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait faire.

decisions.choice: one of the rulers of the Pharisees: a Pharisee of standing, a leader among them
alternatives: an official who ruled the Pharisee movement
decisions.reason: The word means a ruler or leading man. The Pharisees had no single head; Luke means a man of rank among them, perhaps a member of the council, as Nicodemus was (John 3:1).

decisions.choice: to eat bread: to have a meal
decisions.reason: To eat bread is a common way of saying to eat a meal (14:15; Genesis 37:25). A Sabbath meal was cooked the day before, and guests were often invited after the synagogue gathering.

decisions.choice: watching closely: watching to catch him out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the scribes and Pharisees watching Jesus on another Sabbath to find a charge against him (6:7), and of spies watching him (20:20).

decisions.choice: eat a meal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: to see what he would do
decisions.reason: Readable says what the watching was for, as m3 explains.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); "il arriva que" kept at Literal for Luke's "it happened"
decisions.reason: As in Luke 5 and 7: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Jesus's words, the parable of 14:16-24 included, keep the tenses of speech at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ὑδρωπικὸς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a man certain was with dropsy before him.

en.L: And look, there was a certain man in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who had dropsy.
en.B: There in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was a man whose body was swollen with dropsy.
en.R: A man was there in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He had a sickness that made his body swell up with fluid.

fr.L: Et voici, un homme hydropique était devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} se trouvait un homme atteint d’hydropisie, le corps tout enflé.
fr.R: Il y avait là, devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, un homme malade. Sa maladie faisait gonfler son corps, parce que de l’eau s’y accumulait.

decisions.choice: with dropsy: suffering from a swelling of the body caused by fluid gathering in it
decisions.reason: The word is a medical term used only here in the New Testament. Dropsy (now called edema) is a sign of a serious illness, often of the heart, liver or kidneys.

decisions.choice: in front of him: in plain view; Luke does not say how the man came to be there
alternatives: a man placed there by the Pharisees to test Jesus
decisions.reason: The man is not said to be a guest, and he is sent away after he is healed (14:4). Some suggest he was put there to see what Jesus would do, since they were watching him (14:1); the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: a sickness that made his body swell up with fluid
decisions.reason: "Dropsy" is an old word that many readers will not know. Readable describes the illness.

decisions.choice: "hydropique" (L); "atteint d’hydropisie, le corps tout enflé" (B)
decisions.reason: "Hydropique" is the exact French word, but few readers know it; Balanced adds what it means, and Readable describes the illness, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς νομικοὺς καὶ Φαρισαίους λέγων· Ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεῦσαι ἢ οὔ;

records.literal_gloss: And answering, Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful on the Sabbath to heal or not?

en.L: And Jesus answered and spoke to the experts in the law and Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
en.B: Jesus responded by asking the experts in the law and the Pharisees, "Does the law allow healing on the Sabbath, or does it not?"
en.R: Jesus spoke to the experts in God's law and the Pharisees. He asked them, "Does God's law let a person heal someone on the Sabbath day, or not?"

fr.L: Et, prenant la parole, Jésus parla aux experts de la Loi et aux Pharisiens, disant : « Est-il permis, le jour du sabbat, de guérir, ou non ? »
fr.B: Jésus prit la parole et demanda aux experts de la Loi et aux Pharisiens : « La Loi permet-elle de guérir le jour du sabbat, oui ou non ? »
fr.R: Jésus a parlé aux spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu et aux Pharisiens. Il leur a demandé : « Est-ce que la Loi de Dieu permet de guérir quelqu’un le jour du sabbat, ou non ? »

decisions.choice: answering: responding to the situation, though no one had spoken
alternatives: replying to a question someone had asked
decisions.reason: Luke often uses "answered" for a response to what is happening or to unspoken thoughts (5:22; 7:40). Here Jesus answers the silent watching of 14:1.

decisions.choice: experts in the law: scholars trained in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the teachers of the law, the same group he elsewhere calls scribes (7:30; 11:45-52).

decisions.choice: is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath: whether healing counted as work forbidden on the Sabbath
alternatives: whether healing was allowed at all
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers agreed that saving a life overrode the Sabbath, but treating an illness that could wait was debated. Jesus has faced this question before (6:9; 13:14-16).

decisions.choice: experts in God's law
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Luke, Readable says which law is meant.

decisions.choice: Does the law allow (B); Does God's law let (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the question is what the law permits.

decisions.choice: les experts de la Loi (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: As at 7:30 and 10:25: men trained in the law of Moses, kept apart from the scribes ("les scribes", Readable "les spécialistes de la Loi"). Readable adds "de Dieu", as the English does.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἡσύχασαν.

records.literal_gloss: They but were silent.

en.L: But they kept silent.
en.B: But they said nothing.
en.R: But they would not answer.

fr.L: Mais eux se turent.
fr.B: Mais ils ne dirent rien.
fr.R: Mais ils n’ont pas voulu répondre.

decisions.choice: were silent: they would not commit themselves to an answer
decisions.reason: To say yes would allow the healing; to say no would sound heartless. Their silence is a refusal to answer, as in 6:9-11 and 20:26.

decisions.choice: would not answer
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silence meant.

source.text: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος ἰάσατο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπέλυσεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken hold [of him] he healed him and let [him] go.

en.L: And taking hold [of him], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed him and let [him] go.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
en.R: So Jesus took hold of the man and healed him. Then Jesus told him he could go.

fr.L: Et, [le] prenant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le guérit et [le] laissa aller.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit l’homme par la main, le guérit et le laissa partir.
fr.R: Alors Jésus a pris l’homme par la main et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a guéri. Puis Jésus lui a dit qu’il pouvait partir.

decisions.choice: taking hold of him: Jesus touched the man as he healed him
decisions.reason: The verb means to take hold of someone. Jesus often heals with a touch (4:40; 5:13).

decisions.choice: let him go: sent him away, released him
decisions.reason: The verb is used for letting someone leave (8:38). The healed man goes home, and Jesus turns to the guests.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the man so that he is not confused with Jesus.

source.text: καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ πεσεῖται, καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;

records.literal_gloss: And to them he said, Of which of you a son or an ox into a well will fall, and not immediately he will pull up him on [the] day of the Sabbath?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Which of you, [if your] son or ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "If one of you had a son or an ox that fell into a well on the Sabbath, would you not pull him out right away?"
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Suppose your son or your ox fell into a well on the Sabbath day. You would pull him out at once, would you not?"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Lequel d’entre vous, [si] son fils ou [son] bœuf tombe dans un puits, ne l’en retirera pas aussitôt, le jour du sabbat ? »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Si l’un de vous voyait son fils ou son bœuf tomber dans un puits le jour du sabbat, ne l’en tirerait-il pas tout de suite ? »
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit : « Imaginez que votre fils ou votre bœuf tombe dans un puits le jour du sabbat. Vous allez le sortir de là tout de suite, n’est-ce pas ? »

decisions.choice: a son or an ox: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many early manuscripts read "son" here, including some of the oldest papyri and the codex Vaticanus. Others, including the codex Sinaiticus, read "donkey", which matches the ox and donkey of 13:15, and one reads "sheep", as in Matthew 12:11. "Son" is the harder reading, and copyists would more likely change it to an animal than the reverse. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: well: a well or cistern dug deep into the ground
decisions.reason: Wells and cisterns were dug down into the rock to hold water. A child or an animal that fell in could drown and needed to be pulled out at once.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer: every one of you would
alternatives: a real question about what the law allows
decisions.reason: No one would leave a son or even an ox to die because it was the Sabbath. If they would rescue their own on that day, how much more should this man be helped (13:15-16).

decisions.choice: If one of you had ... would you not (B); Suppose ... would you not? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the case first and then ask the question, which is easier to follow.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἀνταποκριθῆναι πρὸς ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: And not they were able to reply to these things.

en.L: And they were not able to reply to these things.
en.B: And they had no answer to give to this.
en.R: They could not say anything against what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

fr.L: Et ils ne purent rien répliquer à cela.
fr.B: Et ils ne trouvèrent rien à répondre à cela.
fr.R: Ils n’ont rien pu dire contre ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit.

decisions.choice: reply: answer back, argue against
decisions.reason: The verb means to answer in return or to speak against (Romans 9:20). They could find nothing to say against him.

decisions.choice: say anything against what he said
decisions.reason: Readable makes the sense of the verb plain.

source.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς κεκλημένους παραβολήν, ἐπέχων πῶς τὰς πρωτοκλισίας ἐξελέγοντο, λέγων πρὸς αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: He was speaking then to those having been invited a parable, noticing how the first places they were choosing, saying to them,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them,
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw how the guests were picking out the places of honor for themselves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them a parable:
en.R: Jesus saw that the guests were choosing the most important places at the table for themselves. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them a lesson from everyday life:

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} disait une parabole aux invités, remarquant comment ils choisissaient les premières places, leur disant :
fr.B: Remarquant que les invités choisissaient pour eux les places d’honneur, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur proposa une parabole :
fr.R: Jésus a vu que les invités choisissaient pour eux-mêmes les places les plus importantes à table. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a donné une leçon tirée de la vie de tous les jours :

decisions.choice: the first places: the places of honor at the table
alternatives: the first places to be served
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests reclined on couches around low tables, and the places nearest the host were the most honored. Where a guest lay showed his rank (11:43; 20:46).

decisions.choice: parable: here a piece of advice drawn from daily life that points to a deeper lesson
decisions.reason: The word covers proverbs, comparisons and stories (4:23; 5:36). This one is advice about where to sit, and its point comes in 14:11.

decisions.choice: noticing: paying attention to
decisions.reason: The verb means to fix one's attention on something (Acts 3:5). Jesus had been watching the guests as they had been watching him (14:1).

decisions.choice: a lesson from everyday life
decisions.reason: This parable is not a story, so Readable describes what it is.

decisions.choice: what Jesus noticed comes first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the cause before the saying it led to.

source.text: Ὅταν κληθῇς ὑπό τινος εἰς γάμους, μὴ κατακλιθῇς εἰς τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν, μήποτε ἐντιμότερός σου ᾖ κεκλημένος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ σὲ καὶ αὐτὸν καλέσας ἐρεῖ σοι· Δὸς τούτῳ τόπον, καὶ τότε ἄρξῃ μετὰ αἰσχύνης τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον κατέχειν.

records.literal_gloss: When you are invited by someone to wedding feasts, not recline in the first place, lest more honorable than you may have been invited by him, \v 9 and having come the [one] you and him having invited will say to you, Give to this one place, and then you will begin with shame the last place to occupy.

en.L: "When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, in case someone more honored than you has been invited by him, \v 9 and the one who invited both you and him comes and says to you, 'Give this one [your] place,' and then with shame you will begin to take the last place.
en.B: "If you are invited to a wedding feast, do not settle yourself in the place of honor. Someone of higher rank than you may be among the guests, \v 9 and the host who invited you both will come over and say, 'Give your place to this guest.' Then, to your shame, you will start down to the lowest place.
en.R: "Suppose someone invites you to a wedding feast. Do not sit down in the most important place. Someone more important than you may have been invited. \v 9 Then the host who invited both of you will come to you and say, 'Give your place to this guest.' You will be ashamed as you get up and move down to the lowest place.

fr.L: « Quand tu es invité par quelqu’un à des noces, ne t’étends pas à la première place, de peur qu’un plus honoré que toi n’ait été invité par lui, \v 9 et que celui qui vous a invités, toi et lui, ne vienne te dire : “Donne la place à celui-ci” ; et alors tu commenceras, avec honte, à occuper la dernière place.
fr.B: « Si quelqu’un t’invite à un repas de mariage, ne va pas t’installer à la place d’honneur. Il se peut qu’un invité plus important que toi soit parmi les convives, \v 9 et celui qui vous a invités tous les deux viendra te dire : “Cède ta place à cet invité.” Alors, couvert de honte, tu devras descendre à la dernière place.
fr.R: « Imagine que quelqu’un t’invite à un repas de mariage. Ne va pas t’asseoir à la place la plus importante. Quelqu’un de plus important que toi a peut-être été invité. \v 9 Alors celui qui vous a invités tous les deux va venir te dire : “Laisse ta place à cet invité.” Tu auras honte, et tu devras te lever pour aller à la dernière place.

decisions.choice: do not take the place of honor: echoes Proverbs 25:6-7
alternatives: new advice with no source in Scripture
decisions.reason: Proverbs advises not to push forward in the king's presence, since it is better to be told to come up higher than to be put lower before a noble. Jesus applies the same wisdom to a wedding feast (14:10).

decisions.choice: wedding feasts: a wedding celebration
decisions.reason: The plural is the usual way of naming the wedding feast, which could last for days (12:36). It was the grandest meal most people would attend, where rank mattered most.

decisions.choice: you will begin to take the last place: by then the places in between are taken, so the guest moves all the way down
alternatives: you will take the last place at the start of the meal
decisions.reason: "Begin" pictures the moment of shame as the guest gets up and goes, in front of everyone, to the only place left.

decisions.choice: settle yourself (B); sit down (R)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches to eat (m1 on 14:7). Literal keeps "recline"; Balanced and Readable use words for taking a place at the table.

decisions.choice: this guest
decisions.reason: The word means "this one". Balanced and Readable call the person a guest.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 14:11
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 14:8-11 are one speech.

decisions.choice: "des noces" (L); "un repas de mariage" (B, R)
alternatives: "un mariage" at every level, as John 2:1
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek plural with the old word "noces"; Balanced and Readable say "repas de mariage", because the advice is about places at the table.

decisions.choice: "ne t’étends pas" (L); "t’installer" (B); "t’asseoir" (R)
decisions.reason: As at 7:36: guests lay on couches to eat, and Literal keeps the picture of reclining; the same in 14:10 and 14:15.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅταν κληθῇς πορευθεὶς ἀνάπεσε εἰς τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον, ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ κεκληκώς σε ἐρεῖ σοι· Φίλε, προσανάβηθι ἀνώτερον· τότε ἔσται σοι δόξα ἐνώπιον πάντων τῶν συνανακειμένων σοι.

records.literal_gloss: But when you are invited, having gone, recline in the last place, so that when comes the [one] having invited you he will say to you, Friend, go up higher; then will be to you glory before all those reclining with you.

en.L: But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, 'Friend, go up higher.' Then you will have honor before all who recline [at table] with you.
en.B: No, when you are invited, go and take the last place at the table, so that when your host comes over he will tell you, 'Friend, move further up.' Then everyone eating with you will see the honor you are given.
en.R: Instead, when someone invites you, go and sit in the lowest place. Then the host will come and say to you, 'My friend, come up here, closer to me.' Everyone at the table will see that you are honored.

fr.L: Mais quand tu es invité, va t’étendre à la dernière place, afin que, quand viendra celui qui t’a invité, il te dise : “Ami, monte plus haut.” Alors ce sera pour toi un honneur devant tous ceux qui sont étendus [à table] avec toi.
fr.B: Au contraire, quand tu es invité, va te mettre à la dernière place, pour qu’à son arrivée celui qui t’a invité te dise : “Mon ami, avance plus haut.” Alors tous ceux qui sont à table avec toi verront l’honneur qui t’est fait.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un t’invite, va plutôt t’asseoir à la dernière place. Alors celui qui t’a invité viendra te dire : “Mon ami, viens ici, plus près de moi.” Et tous les invités verront qu’on t’honore.

decisions.choice: glory: honor, the respect a person has in the eyes of others
decisions.reason: The word that elsewhere names God's glory also means the honor or standing a person has before others (4:6; John 5:44). Here it is the honor of being called up higher before all the guests.

decisions.choice: Friend, go up higher: the words of Proverbs 25:7
alternatives: an ordinary greeting with no echo
decisions.reason: Proverbs says it is better to be told "Come up here" than to be put lower. Jesus' host speaks in the same way.

decisions.choice: friend: a warm and friendly form of address
decisions.reason: The host welcomes the guest who took the low place as a friend.

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: In English "glory" would suggest splendor or praise for God. The sense here is honor before others, as m1 explains.

decisions.choice: come up here, closer to me
decisions.reason: The places nearer the host were higher in honor (m1 on 14:7). Readable says so.

source.text: ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται καὶ ὁ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: For everyone exalting himself will be humbled, and the [one] humbling himself will be exalted.

en.L: For everyone who exalts {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be humbled, and the one who humbles {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be exalted."
en.B: For everyone who lifts {{gender:themselves|himself}} up will be brought low, and the one who takes the low place will be lifted up."
en.R: Anyone who puts {{gender:themselves|himself}} above others will be brought down. But anyone who is humble will be lifted up."

fr.L: Car celui qui s’élève lui-même sera abaissé, et celui qui s’abaisse lui-même sera élevé. »
fr.B: Car celui qui se hausse sera rabaissé, et celui qui prend la dernière place sera élevé. »
fr.R: Celui qui se met au-dessus des autres sera rabaissé. Mais celui qui reste humble sera élevé. »

decisions.choice: will be humbled ... will be exalted: God will bring down and lift up
alternatives: other people will notice and change their minds
decisions.reason: The passive verbs point to God, who reverses human rank (1:52; 18:14). The advice about seating becomes a word about how God judges.

decisions.choice: for: this saying gives the reason for the advice of 14:8-10
alternatives: a new saying with no link
decisions.reason: The point is not a clever way to win honor at dinner, but the rule by which God deals with the proud and the humble.

decisions.choice: lifts themselves up ... takes the low place (B); puts themselves above others ... is humble (R)
decisions.reason: As in 18:14, Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the two opposite ways of acting.

decisions.choice: themselves as the default, himself as the alternative
decisions.reason: The saying applies to everyone, man or woman.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "celui qui s’élève lui-même"
alternatives: a gender span on the reflexive, as the English "themselves|himself"
decisions.reason: English puts the reflexive under the gender setting. In French "celui qui" and the "lui-même" that refers back to it are ordinary generic French and already include everyone, so the style guide adds no span. The same in 14:26-35.

source.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying then also to the [one] having invited him, When you make a lunch or a dinner, not call the friends of you nor the brothers of you nor the relatives of you nor neighbors rich, lest also they invite you in return and it become repayment to you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also said to the one who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends or your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} or your relatives or rich neighbors, in case they also invite you in return and it becomes a repayment to you.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} host as well, "When you put on a lunch or a dinner, do not ask your friends, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, your relatives, or your wealthy neighbors. They might ask you back, and that would be your repayment.
en.R: Jesus also spoke to the man who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the meal. He said, "When you have people over for a meal, do not invite your friends, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, your relatives, or your rich neighbors. They may ask you to come to their homes too. That way you would be paid back for your meal.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} disait aussi à celui qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait invité : « Quand tu donnes un déjeuner ou un dîner, n’appelle pas tes amis, ni tes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, ni ta parenté, ni des voisins riches, de peur qu’eux aussi ne t’invitent en retour et que cela ne te soit rendu.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit aussi à celui qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait invité : « Quand tu offres un déjeuner ou un dîner, n’invite pas tes amis, tes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, ta famille ou tes riches voisins. Ils pourraient t’inviter à leur tour, et tu serais ainsi payé de retour.
fr.R: Jésus a parlé aussi à l’homme qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait invité à ce repas. Il lui a dit : « Quand tu reçois des gens pour un repas, n’invite pas tes amis, tes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, le reste de ta famille ou tes voisins riches. Eux aussi pourraient t’inviter chez eux. Ainsi, on te rendrait ce que tu as donné.

decisions.choice: a lunch or a dinner: a midday meal or an evening meal, so any meal a person hosts
decisions.reason: The first word was a late morning or midday meal, the second the main meal of the day, eaten toward evening. Together they mean any meal.

decisions.choice: they invite you in return: meals were part of a system of returning favors
alternatives: a simple matter of good manners
decisions.reason: Inviting those who could invite you back kept up a circle of obligation and honor among equals. Jesus calls his host to give where nothing can come back.

decisions.choice: do not call: a plain command, set against the command of 14:13
alternatives: a ban on ever eating with family and friends
decisions.reason: The form is a plain prohibition. The contrast is between hosting to be repaid and hosting those who cannot repay (14:14). Elsewhere Luke tells of feasts with friends and neighbors without blame (15:6, 9, 23-24).

decisions.choice: brothers: brothers and sisters, the host's siblings
decisions.reason: The plural is often used of a family's children, male and female. Here it stands among friends and relatives.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters as the default, brothers as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word includes sisters here (m4).

decisions.choice: you would be paid back for your meal
alternatives: it would become a repayment to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the repayment would be.

decisions.choice: "celui qui l’avait invité" (B), not "son hôte"
decisions.reason: French "hôte" means both host and guest, so Balanced names the host by what he did.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·

records.literal_gloss: But when a reception you make, call [the] poor, crippled, lame, blind;

en.L: But when you give a banquet, call the poor, the crippled, the lame, [and] the blind;
en.B: Instead, when you hold a feast, ask the poor to come, and those who are maimed, lame, or blind.
en.R: Instead, when you give a big meal, invite poor people. Invite people whose bodies are crippled, people who cannot walk, and people who cannot see.

fr.L: Mais quand tu donnes une réception, appelle des pauvres, des estropiés, des boiteux, des aveugles ;
fr.B: Au contraire, quand tu donnes un festin, invite les pauvres, les infirmes, les boiteux et les aveugles.
fr.R: Au contraire, quand tu fais un grand repas, invite des pauvres. Invite des gens dont le corps est infirme, des gens qui ne peuvent pas marcher et des gens qui ne voient pas.

decisions.choice: the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind: people who could not repay and were often pushed to the edges
decisions.reason: Many such people lived by begging (16:20; 18:35). They are the people Jesus came to bring good news to (4:18; 7:22), and the same list appears in the parable that follows (14:21).

decisions.choice: banquet: a reception, a meal with many guests
decisions.reason: Levi gave this kind of large meal for Jesus (5:29).

decisions.choice: crippled: maimed, disabled in body
decisions.reason: The word means a person with a damaged or missing limb. The next word, "lame", is about being unable to walk.

decisions.choice: maimed
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word that keeps the two conditions apart.

decisions.choice: people whose bodies are crippled, people who cannot walk, and people who cannot see
alternatives: the crippled, the lame, the blind
decisions.reason: Readable describes each group in plain words.

source.text: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.

records.literal_gloss: and blessed you will be, because not they have to repay you; it will be repaid for to you in the resurrection of the righteous.

en.L: and you will be blessed, because they do not have [anything] to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
en.B: And you will be blessed, for they have no way to pay you back. Your repayment will come at the resurrection of the righteous."
en.R: Then God will bless you, because these people have nothing to give you back. God will repay you at the time when those who are right with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} rise from the dead."

fr.L: et tu seras heureux, parce qu’ils n’ont pas de quoi te rendre ; car cela te sera rendu à la résurrection des justes. »
fr.B: Et tu seras heureux, car ils n’ont pas les moyens de te rendre la pareille. Tu en seras payé à la résurrection des justes. »
fr.R: Alors Dieu te rendra heureux, parce que ces gens n’ont rien à te rendre. Dieu te le rendra au moment où ceux qui sont en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} reviendront à la vie. »

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for those whom God favors (6:20-22). The blessing comes from God, not from the guests.

decisions.choice: you will be repaid: God will repay
alternatives: the guests will repay you later
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, who repays what the poor cannot.

decisions.choice: the resurrection of the righteous: the raising of God's people from the dead at the last day
alternatives: a resurrection only for some people, with no judgment for others
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of a resurrection of the righteous and of the unrighteous (Daniel 12:2; Acts 24:15). Jesus speaks here of the reward of those who are right with God.

decisions.choice: God will bless you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses (m1).

decisions.choice: the time when those who are right with him rise from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable explains both words of the phrase.

decisions.choice: "heureux" (L, B); "Dieu te rendra heureux" (R)
decisions.reason: As at 6:20 and 7:23: the word means favoured by God (m1), and French says it with "heureux"; "béni" belongs to another Greek word. Readable names God, as the English Readable does. The same in 14:15.

source.text: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then one of those reclining with [him] these things said to him, Blessed whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God.

en.L: And when one of those reclining [at table] with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] heard these things, he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed [is] whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God!"
en.B: One of the guests at the table heard this and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed is anyone who will sit at the table in the kingdom of God!"
en.R: One of the guests heard what Jesus said. He said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed are those who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God!"

fr.L: Or l’un de ceux qui étaient étendus [à table] avec [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], ayant entendu cela, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Heureux celui qui mangera du pain dans le royaume de Dieu ! »
fr.B: Entendant cela, l’un de ceux qui étaient à table {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Heureux celui qui prendra place à table dans le royaume de Dieu ! »
fr.R: Un des invités a entendu ce que Jésus disait. Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Quel bonheur pour ceux qui mangeront au grand repas dans le royaume de Dieu ! »

decisions.choice: eat bread: share in the meal
decisions.reason: As in 14:1, to eat bread is to have a meal.

decisions.choice: eating in the kingdom of God: the great feast God will give at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The prophets pictured God's coming reign as a rich feast for all peoples (Isaiah 25:6). Jesus spoke of people coming from every direction to recline at table in the kingdom of God (13:29).

decisions.choice: the guest's words: a pious saying that the parable answers
decisions.reason: The guest speaks of the blessing of being at God's feast. The parable that follows asks who will actually accept the invitation.

decisions.choice: sit at the table (B); eat at the feast (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "le royaume de Dieu"
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet: "le royaume de Dieu" at every level, as in Luke 7 and 10.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς, καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: He but said to him, A man certain was making a supper great, and invited many, \v 17 and sent the slave of him at the hour of the supper to say to those having been invited, Come, because now ready it is.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "A certain man was giving a great dinner, and he invited many. \v 17 And at the hour of the dinner he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, for [everything] is now ready.'
en.B: He answered him, "Once a man was putting on a large dinner, and he had asked many people to it. \v 17 When the hour of the dinner arrived, he sent his servant out to say to the guests he had asked, 'Come, it is all ready now.'
en.R: Jesus answered, "A man once planned a big dinner and invited many people. \v 17 When the time came to eat, he sent his servant to tell the guests, 'Come! Everything is ready now.'

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Un homme donnait un grand dîner, et il en a invité beaucoup. \v 17 Et il a envoyé son esclave, à l’heure du dîner, dire aux invités : “Venez, car [tout] est déjà prêt.”
fr.B: Il lui répondit : « Un homme préparait un grand dîner, et il avait invité beaucoup de monde. \v 17 À l’heure du dîner, il a envoyé son serviteur dire aux invités : “Venez, tout est prêt maintenant.”
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Un homme avait prévu un grand dîner et il avait invité beaucoup de gens. \v 17 Quand l’heure du repas est arrivée, il a envoyé son serviteur dire aux invités : “Venez ! Tout est prêt maintenant.”

decisions.choice: two invitations: guests were asked ahead of time and then called when the meal was ready
decisions.reason: A host sent word ahead so that he knew how much food to prepare, and sent again at the hour to call the guests (compare Esther 5:8; 6:14). Those who had accepted the first invitation were expected to come.

decisions.choice: slave: a household slave who carried his master's messages
decisions.reason: The word means a slave, a person owned by a master. Calling the guests was one of a household slave's tasks.

decisions.choice: the dinner: a picture of God's invitation to the feast of his kingdom
decisions.reason: The parable answers the guest's words about eating in the kingdom of God (14:15). The man in the story stands for God, who calls people to his feast; the story itself speaks only of a host.

decisions.choice: everything (L in brackets); it is all (B); Everything (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has a plural, "[things] are ready", meaning the whole meal.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 14:24
decisions.reason: The parable in 14:16-24 is one speech, with the words of people in the story set inside it.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: the parable told in the passé composé at every level ("il a envoyé", "ils ont commencé"), with the imperfect for the setting
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The parable is Jesus's spoken words, and French speech tells past events in the passé composé, as the style guide asks and as Luke 10 and 15 do.

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's pair, as in Luke 7 and 15; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that he was owned. The same throughout 14:16-24.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And they began from one all to excuse themselves.

en.L: And they all began, as with one [voice], to make excuses.
en.B: But all of them alike began to ask to be excused.
en.R: But every one of them began to give reasons why they could not come.

fr.L: Et ils ont tous commencé, comme d’une seule [voix], à s’excuser.
fr.B: Mais tous, de la même façon, ont commencé à se faire excuser.
fr.R: Mais chacun d’eux a commencé à donner des raisons pour ne pas venir.

decisions.choice: from one: all alike, with one mind
decisions.reason: The phrase has a feminine form with no noun, as if "voice" or "mind" were left out. It most likely means that they all did the same thing.

decisions.choice: to excuse themselves: to ask to be let off, to decline
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask to be excused from something already agreed (Acts 25:11).

decisions.choice: voice
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a noun so the phrase makes sense in English.

source.text: ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

records.literal_gloss: The first said to him, A field I have bought, and I have need having gone out to see it; I ask you, have me excused.

en.L: The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I need to go out and see it. I ask you, consider me excused.'
en.B: The first told him, 'I have bought a piece of land, and I have to go out and look at it. I am asking you to excuse me.'
en.R: The first one said, 'I have bought a field. I have to go out and look at it. Please tell your master I am sorry I cannot come.'

fr.L: Le premier lui a dit : “J’ai acheté un champ, et j’ai besoin de sortir le voir. Je te prie, tiens-moi pour excusé.”
fr.B: Le premier lui a dit : “J’ai acheté un terrain, et je dois aller le voir. Je te prie de m’excuser.”
fr.R: Le premier a dit : “J’ai acheté un champ. Je dois aller le voir. S’il te plaît, dis à ton maître que je regrette de ne pas pouvoir venir.”

decisions.choice: the excuse is weak: the field would still be there the next day
decisions.reason: The guest had already accepted the first invitation (m1 on 14:16). Turning the host down at the hour of the meal put him to shame.

decisions.choice: have me excused: a polite formula for declining
decisions.reason: The words are courteous, but the guest still refuses to come.

decisions.choice: Please tell your master I am sorry I cannot come.
alternatives: I ask you, consider me excused
decisions.reason: Readable says what the polite formula means in this setting.

source.text: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

records.literal_gloss: And another said, Yokes of oxen I have bought five, and I am going to test them; I ask you, have me excused.

en.L: And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. I ask you, consider me excused.'
en.B: Another said, 'I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am on my way to test them. I am asking you to excuse me.'
en.R: Another man said, 'I have bought ten oxen to pull my plows. I am going out to see how well they work. Please tell your master I am sorry.'

fr.L: Et un autre a dit : “J’ai acheté cinq attelages de bœufs, et je vais les essayer. Je te prie, tiens-moi pour excusé.”
fr.B: Un autre a dit : “J’ai acheté cinq paires de bœufs, et je pars les essayer. Je te prie de m’excuser.”
fr.R: Un autre homme a dit : “J’ai acheté dix bœufs pour tirer mes charrues. Je vais voir s’ils travaillent bien. S’il te plaît, dis à ton maître que je regrette.”

decisions.choice: five yoke of oxen: ten oxen, five plowing teams
decisions.reason: Oxen worked in pairs under a yoke. Ten oxen mark a large farm and a wealthy man, and testing them could have waited.

decisions.choice: pairs
decisions.reason: Balanced says "pairs" so the number is clear.

decisions.choice: ten oxen to pull my plows
decisions.reason: Readable gives the number of animals and what they were for.

source.text: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And another said, A wife I have married, and because of this not I am able to come.

en.L: And another said, 'I have married a wife, and for this reason I cannot come.'
en.B: And another said, 'I have taken a wife, and that is why I am not able to come.'
en.R: Another said, 'I have a new wife. That is why I cannot come.'

fr.L: Et un autre a dit : “J’ai épousé une femme, et c’est pourquoi je ne peux pas venir.”
fr.B: Un autre a dit : “Je me suis marié, et c’est pour cela que je ne peux pas venir.”
fr.R: Un autre a dit : “Je viens de me marier. C’est pour cela que je ne peux pas venir.”

decisions.choice: I have married a wife: perhaps an echo of the law that freed a new husband from duty
decisions.reason: The law of Moses freed a newly married man from war and other duties for a year (Deuteronomy 24:5; 20:7). That law did not cover a dinner, and this guest does not even ask to be excused.

decisions.choice: a new wife
decisions.reason: The past tense means the marriage is recent; Readable says so.

source.text: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: And having come the slave reported to the master of him these things.

en.L: And the slave came and reported these things to his master.
en.B: The servant came back and told his master all of this.
en.R: The servant went back and told his master what everyone had said.

fr.L: Et l’esclave, à son retour, a rapporté cela à son maître.
fr.B: Le serviteur est revenu et a raconté tout cela à son maître.
fr.R: Le serviteur est rentré et il a dit à son maître ce que tout le monde avait répondu.

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the slave and host of the dinner
decisions.reason: The word means lord or master. In a parable about a household it is the slave's owner.

decisions.choice: what everyone had said
decisions.reason: Readable says what the servant reported.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ· Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: Then having become angry the master of the house said to the slave of him, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and the poor and crippled and blind and lame bring in here.

en.L: Then the master of the house became angry and said to his slave, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.'
en.B: At that the owner of the house was angry, and he said to his servant, 'Hurry out into the squares and alleys of the town, and bring the poor, the maimed, the blind, and the lame in here.'
en.R: The owner of the house was angry. He told his servant, 'Hurry! Go out to the wide streets and the narrow side streets in town. Find the poor people and those who are crippled or blind or cannot walk. Bring them here.'

fr.L: Alors le maître de maison, en colère, a dit à son esclave : “Sors vite dans les places et les ruelles de la ville, et amène ici les pauvres, et les estropiés, et les aveugles, et les boiteux.”
fr.B: Le maître de maison s’est alors mis en colère et a dit à son serviteur : “Va vite sur les places et dans les ruelles de la ville, et amène ici les pauvres, les infirmes, les aveugles et les boiteux.”
fr.R: Le maître de la maison s’est mis en colère. Il a dit à son serviteur : “Dépêche-toi ! Va dans les grandes rues et dans les petites rues de la ville. Trouve les pauvres, et les gens qui sont infirmes, aveugles ou qui ne peuvent pas marcher. Amène-les ici.”

decisions.choice: angry: angered by the insult
decisions.reason: The refusals at the last moment shamed the host before the town (m1 on 14:18).

decisions.choice: streets and lanes: the wide streets and squares and the narrow alleys of the town
decisions.reason: The first word is a broad street or open square, the second a narrow lane. The slave is to search the whole town, where the poor would be found.

decisions.choice: the poor, crippled, blind and lame: the same people Jesus told his host to invite
decisions.reason: The master in the story does what Jesus told the Pharisee to do (14:13).

decisions.choice: maimed
decisions.reason: As in 14:13.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος· Κύριε, γέγονεν ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: And said the slave, Master, has been done what you commanded, and still room there is.

en.L: And the slave said, 'Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.'
en.B: Then the servant said, 'Master, your order has been carried out, and there are still empty places.'
en.R: Later the servant said, 'Master, I have done what you told me. But there is still room for more people.'

fr.L: Et l’esclave a dit : “Maître, ce que tu as ordonné a été fait, et il y a encore de la place.”
fr.B: Puis le serviteur a dit : “Maître, ton ordre a été exécuté, et il reste encore des places.”
fr.R: Plus tard, le serviteur a dit : “Maître, j’ai fait ce que tu m’as dit. Mais il y a encore de la place pour d’autres gens.”

decisions.choice: Master: the slave addresses his owner
decisions.reason: The same word means "master" in 14:21 and 14:23. Here the slave speaks to the man who owns him.

decisions.choice: has been done: the order has already been carried out
decisions.reason: The tense shows the work is finished. The story passes over the time it took.

decisions.choice: Later
decisions.reason: Readable shows that time has passed while the servant carried out the order (m2).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "Maître"
decisions.reason: A slave speaks to his owner (m1), as the worker to the owner at 13:8. "Maître" is the French word for a servant's master; "Seigneur" would read as a prayer.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον· Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ μου ὁ οἶκος·

records.literal_gloss: And said the master to the slave, Go out into the roads and hedges and compel [them] to come in, so that may be filled of me the house;

en.L: And the master said to the slave, 'Go out into the roads and hedges and compel [people] to come in, so that my house may be filled.
en.B: The master told the servant, 'Go out to the country roads and the hedgerows, and press people to come in, so that my house will be full.
en.R: Then the master told the servant, 'Go out of town to the roads and the paths along the hedges. Urge people to come in, and do not take no for an answer. I want my house to be full.

fr.L: Et le maître a dit à l’esclave : “Sors sur les routes et le long des haies, et contrains [les gens] à entrer, afin que ma maison soit remplie.
fr.B: Le maître a dit au serviteur : “Va sur les chemins de campagne et le long des haies, et insiste pour que les gens entrent, afin que ma maison soit pleine.
fr.R: Alors le maître a dit au serviteur : “Sors de la ville. Va sur les routes et sur les chemins le long des haies. Insiste pour que les gens viennent, et n’accepte pas qu’on te dise non. Je veux que ma maison soit pleine.

decisions.choice: compel: urge strongly, press someone who would hang back
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to force, but it is also used of pressing an invitation on someone (Matthew 14:22; Galatians 2:14). People from outside the town would not believe the invitation was meant for them and, as custom expected, would decline at first (compare 24:29, where the disciples urge Jesus to stay). In later centuries this verse was used to justify forcing people into the church, which the story does not describe.

decisions.choice: roads and hedges: the country roads and the walls or hedges along them outside the town
decisions.reason: The first search covered the town (14:21). Now the slave goes beyond it, to travelers and to people who lived and slept along the roads and fences.

decisions.choice: the second sending: the invitation reaches those furthest away
decisions.reason: Many readers see here a hint that the gospel would go out beyond Israel to the nations, as it does in Acts (Acts 13:46). The parable itself only says that the master will have his house filled.

decisions.choice: press people to come in (B); urge people to come in, and do not take no for an answer (R)
decisions.reason: "Compel" in English suggests force. Balanced and Readable give the sense of a pressed invitation (m1); Literal keeps "compel".

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The Greek has no object; English needs one.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ δείπνου.

records.literal_gloss: I say for to you that not one of the men those having been invited will taste of me the supper.

en.L: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.'"
en.B: For I tell you all, not a single one of the men I first invited will taste my dinner.'"
en.R: I tell you, the men I invited before will not eat even a bite of my dinner.'"

fr.L: Car, je vous le dis, aucun de ces hommes qui avaient été invités ne goûtera à mon dîner.” »
fr.B: Car, je vous le dis, pas un seul des hommes que j’avais invités d’abord ne goûtera à mon dîner.” »
fr.R: Je vous le dis : les hommes que j’avais invités avant ne mangeront pas la moindre bouchée de mon dîner.” »

decisions.choice: I tell you: the master is still speaking, but "you" is plural
alternatives: Jesus speaking to his hearers in his own voice
decisions.reason: "My dinner" suits the master, and the saying ends his words. Yet "you" is plural, as if he spoke past the slave to all who could hear, and "I tell you" is how Jesus himself often speaks (11:8; 15:7). Hearers at the Pharisee's table could take the words as a warning from Jesus about God's feast.

decisions.choice: will taste: will have any share at all
decisions.reason: Not even a taste of the meal will reach those who refused.

decisions.choice: men: the male guests first invited
decisions.reason: The word means adult men. Guests at such a dinner were men, and the story uses the word for them.

decisions.choice: you all
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that "you" is plural (m1).

decisions.choice: I first invited (B); I invited before (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which guests are meant.

decisions.choice: "vous" after the master's "tu" to the slave
alternatives: "je vous le dis à tous" (B), as the English "you all"
decisions.reason: The Greek "you" is plural here (m1). French shows the change from "tu" to "vous" by itself, so Balanced needs no added "à tous".

source.text: Συνεπορεύοντο δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: Were going with then him crowds great, and having turned he said to them,

en.L: Now great crowds were traveling with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and turning, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.B: Many crowds were walking along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He turned around and said to them,
en.R: Big crowds were walking along the road with Jesus. Jesus turned around and said to them,

fr.L: Or de grandes foules faisaient route avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et, se retournant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit :
fr.B: De grandes foules marchaient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il se retourna et leur dit :
fr.R: De grandes foules marchaient sur la route avec Jésus. Jésus s’est retourné et leur a dit :

decisions.choice: crowds traveling with him: people going along on the journey to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Since 9:51 Jesus has been on the road to Jerusalem. Many went along with him, and here he tells them what following him will really cost.

decisions.choice: having turned: he turned to face the crowd behind him
decisions.reason: Luke often notes that Jesus turned to speak to people following him (7:9; 9:55; 23:28).

source.text: Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρός με καὶ οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τὰς ἀδελφάς, ἔτι τε καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone comes to me and not hates the father of himself and the mother and the wife and the children and the brothers and the sisters, and also even the life of himself, not he is able to be of me disciple.

en.L: "If anyone comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and does not hate {{gender:their|his}} own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even {{gender:their|his}} own life, {{gender:they|he}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.
en.B: "No one can be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple who comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} without hating {{gender:their|his}} father and mother, {{gender:their|his}} wife and children, {{gender:their|his}} brothers and sisters, and even {{gender:their|his}} own life.
en.R: "If anyone wants to follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} must love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} far more than {{gender:their|his}} father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters. {{gender:They|He}} must love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than {{gender:their|his}} own life. If not, {{gender:they|he}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.

fr.L: « Si quelqu’un vient à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et ne hait pas son propre père, et sa mère, et sa femme, et ses enfants, et ses frères, et ses sœurs, et même encore sa propre vie, il ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.
fr.B: « Personne ne peut être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple s’il vient à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} sans haïr son père et sa mère, sa femme et ses enfants, ses frères et ses sœurs, et jusqu’à sa propre vie.
fr.R: « Si quelqu’un veut {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivre, il doit {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimer bien plus que son père et sa mère, sa femme et ses enfants, ses frères et ses sœurs. Il doit {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimer plus que sa propre vie. Sinon, il ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.

decisions.choice: hate: love less by comparison, put second
decisions.reason: In Hebrew and Aramaic speech, to love one and hate another can mean to prefer one over the other. Jacob "hated" Leah in that he loved Rachel more (Genesis 29:30-31), and God "loved" Jacob and "hated" Esau (Malachi 1:2-3). Matthew 10:37 gives the same teaching as loving family more than Jesus. The strong word shows that no tie may come before following him; it does not command ill will toward family.

decisions.choice: life: one's own life, one's very self
decisions.reason: The word can mean life or soul. Here it is the disciple's own life, which may have to be given up (9:24; 17:33).

decisions.choice: comes to me: comes as one who would follow
decisions.reason: The crowds were already walking with Jesus (14:25). To come to him here means to come as a disciple.

decisions.choice: wife: the list is spoken as to a man, but the call is to anyone
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "anyone". The list follows the ordinary household of the time, with a man at its head.

decisions.choice: must love me far more than
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal and Balanced keep the strong word, with a footnote.

decisions.choice: their / they as the default, his / he as the alternative
decisions.reason: The call is to anyone, man or woman (m4).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 14:35
decisions.reason: Jesus' words to the crowd in 14:26-35 are one speech.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "Si quelqu’un ... son père ... il ne peut pas"
decisions.reason: English puts "their|his" and "they|he" under the gender setting. French "quelqu’un", "personne" and the "il", "son", "sa" that refer back to them are ordinary generic French and include everyone, so the style guide adds no span. The same in 14:27 and 14:33.

source.text: ὅστις οὐ βαστάζει τὸν σταυρὸν ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ἔρχεται ὀπίσω μου, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever not carries the cross of himself and comes after me, not is able to be my disciple.

en.L: Whoever does not carry {{gender:their|his}} own cross and come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.
en.B: Unless a person carries {{gender:their|his}} own cross and walks behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.
en.R: If anyone will not carry {{gender:their|his}} own cross and follow behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple. To carry a cross meant being on the way to die.

fr.L: Quiconque ne porte pas sa propre croix et ne vient pas derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.
fr.B: Celui qui ne porte pas sa croix pour marcher derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un ne veut pas porter sa propre croix et marcher derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple. Porter une croix, cela voulait dire être en route vers la mort.

decisions.choice: carry his own cross: carry the crossbeam like a condemned man on the way to execution
decisions.reason: A man condemned to crucifixion carried his cross to the place where he would die (23:26; John 19:17). The disciple must be ready to suffer and even die for following Jesus (9:23).

decisions.choice: carries: an ongoing way of life
decisions.reason: The present tense describes something done day after day, as 9:23 says, "daily".

decisions.choice: comes after me: follows as a disciple
decisions.reason: To come after someone is to follow them as a disciple (9:23).

decisions.choice: To carry a cross meant being on the way to die.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

source.text: τίς γὰρ ἐξ ὑμῶν θέλων πύργον οἰκοδομῆσαι οὐχὶ πρῶτον καθίσας ψηφίζει τὴν δαπάνην, εἰ ἔχει εἰς ἀπαρτισμόν;

records.literal_gloss: Which for of you wanting a tower to build not first having sat down counts the cost, whether he has for completion?

en.L: For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether {{gender:they have|he has}} [enough] for [its] completion?
en.B: If any of you planned to build a tower, would you not sit down first and add up the expense, to find out whether you could afford to finish it?
en.R: If one of you wanted to build a tower, you would first sit down and figure out how much it would cost. You would want to know if you had enough money to finish it.

fr.L: Car lequel d’entre vous, voulant bâtir une tour, ne s’assied pas d’abord pour calculer la dépense, [pour voir] s’il a de quoi [la] terminer ?
fr.B: Si vous vouliez construire une tour, ne commenceriez-vous pas par vous asseoir pour calculer la dépense, afin de savoir si vous avez de quoi l’achever ?
fr.R: Si vous voulez construire une tour, vous allez d’abord vous asseoir pour calculer combien elle coûtera. Vous voudrez savoir si vous avez assez d’argent pour la terminer.

decisions.choice: tower: a watchtower in a field or vineyard, or a tower on a building
decisions.reason: Farmers built towers to guard vineyards and crops (Isaiah 5:2; Mark 12:1). Any hearer could picture the cost of such a building.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer: every one of you would
decisions.reason: No sensible builder starts without first adding up the cost.

decisions.choice: count the cost: the hearers must weigh what following Jesus will demand
decisions.reason: The tower and the king (14:31-32) are pictures. The point comes in 14:33.

decisions.choice: If any of you ... would you not (B); If one of you ... you would (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question to speak to the hearers directly, and Readable makes it a statement.

decisions.choice: enough money
alternatives: what is needed for its completion
decisions.reason: Readable says what the builder needs.

source.text: ἵνα μήποτε θέντος αὐτοῦ θεμέλιον καὶ μὴ ἰσχύοντος ἐκτελέσαι πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντες ἄρξωνται αὐτῷ ἐμπαίζειν λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἤρξατο οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἐκτελέσαι.

records.literal_gloss: so that lest, he having laid of it a foundation and not being able to finish, all those seeing begin him to mock, \v 30 saying, This the man began to build and not was able to finish.

en.L: Otherwise, when the foundation is laid and {{gender:they are|he is}} not able to finish, all who see [it] may begin to mock {{gender:them|him}}, \v 30 saying, '{{gender:This person|This man}} began to build and was not able to finish.'
en.B: If you lay the foundation and cannot finish the job, everyone who sees it will start to make fun of you. \v 30 They will say, 'Here is someone who started to build and could not finish.'
en.R: If not, you might lay the foundation and then run out of money. Then everyone who sees it will laugh at you. \v 30 They will say, 'This person started to build, but could not finish!'

fr.L: Sinon, quand il aura posé les fondations et ne pourra pas achever, tous ceux qui [le] verront commenceront à se moquer de lui, \v 30 en disant : “{{gender:Cette personne|Cet homme}} a commencé à bâtir et n’a pas pu achever.”
fr.B: Si vous posez les fondations sans pouvoir achever le travail, tous ceux qui le verront se mettront à se moquer de vous. \v 30 Ils diront : “Voilà quelqu’un qui a commencé à bâtir et qui n’a pas pu achever.”
fr.R: Sinon, vous allez peut-être poser les fondations, et puis vous n’aurez plus d’argent. Alors tous ceux qui verront cela vont se moquer de vous. \v 30 Ils diront : “Celui-là a commencé à construire, mais il n’a pas pu finir !”

decisions.choice: lest: this is what counting the cost prevents
decisions.reason: The clause gives the purpose of sitting down first (14:28): to avoid being left with a foundation and nothing more.

decisions.choice: mock: make fun of, scorn
decisions.reason: In a culture that valued honor, an unfinished building stood as a public sign of foolishness.

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep speaking to the hearers, as they do in 14:28.

decisions.choice: run out of money
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely reason, which follows from 14:28.

decisions.choice: this person / someone as the default, this man as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, and the builder stands for any hearer.

decisions.choice: "Cette personne" by default, "Cet homme" as the alternative, on the noun only (L)
alternatives: spans on "il" and "lui" as well, as the English "they are|he is", "them|him"
decisions.reason: The setting goes on the noun French has to choose, where the Greek has the word for a human being; the "il" and "lui" before it refer back to "lequel d’entre vous" and are generic French. Balanced and Readable need no noun ("quelqu’un", "celui-là").

source.text: ἢ τίς βασιλεὺς πορευόμενος ἑτέρῳ βασιλεῖ συμβαλεῖν εἰς πόλεμον οὐχὶ καθίσας πρῶτον βουλεύσεται εἰ δυνατός ἐστιν ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν ὑπαντῆσαι τῷ μετὰ εἴκοσι χιλιάδων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Or what king going with another king to engage in war, not having sat down first will take counsel whether able he is with ten thousand to meet the [one] with twenty thousand coming against him?

en.L: Or what king, going to engage another king in war, will not sit down first and take counsel whether he is able with 10,000 to meet the one coming against him with 20,000?
en.B: Or what king sets out to fight another king without first sitting down to weigh whether his 10,000 troops can stand against an enemy who comes with 20,000?
en.R: Or think about a king who is about to go to war against another king. He has 10,000 soldiers, and the other king has 20,000. Before he starts, he will sit down and think carefully. Can his 10,000 soldiers fight off the 20,000 who are coming against him?

fr.L: Ou quel roi, partant faire la guerre à un autre roi, ne s’assiéra pas d’abord pour délibérer s’il est capable, avec 10 000, d’affronter celui qui vient contre lui avec 20 000 ?
fr.B: Ou bien, quel roi part en guerre contre un autre roi sans s’asseoir d’abord pour examiner si, avec 10 000 soldats, il peut tenir tête à l’ennemi qui marche contre lui avec 20 000 ?
fr.R: Ou bien pensez à un roi qui va faire la guerre à un autre roi. Il a 10 000 soldats, et l’autre roi en a 20 000. Avant de commencer, il va s’asseoir et bien réfléchir. Est-ce que ses 10 000 soldats peuvent repousser les 20 000 qui viennent l’attaquer ?

decisions.choice: take counsel: think it through carefully, perhaps with advisers
decisions.reason: The verb means to deliberate or plan. A king would weigh the matter before risking his army.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer: every king would
decisions.reason: As with the builder (14:28), no wise king marches out without weighing his chances.

decisions.choice: 10,000 against 20,000: an army facing twice its number
decisions.reason: The numbers are a picture of a force much weaker than its enemy.

decisions.choice: the case is set out first, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long question into short sentences.
The style guide writes numbers above "cent" in figures, as at 7:41; French separates thousands with a narrow space, not a comma.

source.text: εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἔτι αὐτοῦ πόρρω ὄντος πρεσβείαν ἀποστείλας ἐρωτᾷ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην.

records.literal_gloss: If but not, still of him far off being, a delegation having sent he asks the [things] for peace.

en.L: And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for the [terms] of peace.
en.B: If he cannot, then while the other king is still a long way off, he will send envoys to ask how peace can be made.
en.R: If he decides he cannot win, he will send some men to the other king while that king is still far away. They will ask what they must do to make peace.

fr.L: Sinon, tandis que l’autre est encore loin, il envoie une ambassade et demande les [conditions] de paix.
fr.B: S’il ne le peut pas, il enverra une délégation, pendant que l’autre roi est encore loin, pour demander comment faire la paix.
fr.R: S’il pense qu’il ne peut pas gagner, il va envoyer quelques hommes vers l’autre roi pendant que ce roi est encore loin. Ils vont demander ce qu’il faut faire pour avoir la paix.

decisions.choice: the things for peace: the terms on which the war can be avoided
decisions.reason: To ask for the things that make for peace is to seek terms. For the weaker king that means accepting what the stronger one demands.

decisions.choice: delegation: a group of envoys sent to speak for the king
decisions.reason: The word means an embassy, envoys sent as a body (19:14).

decisions.choice: him: the other king, the one coming against him
decisions.reason: The phrase "while he is still far off" refers to the advancing enemy.

decisions.choice: the other (L); the other king (B); that king (R)
decisions.reason: English names the other king so that the two kings are not confused (m3).

decisions.choice: If he decides he cannot win
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king concluded.

source.text: οὕτως οὖν πᾶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποτάσσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.

records.literal_gloss: So therefore everyone of you who not renounces all his own possessions, not is able to be my disciple.

en.L: So then, every one of you who does not renounce all {{gender:their|his}} own possessions cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.
en.B: So it is with you: whoever does not let go of all that {{gender:they have|he has}} cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.
en.R: In the same way, any of you who will not leave behind everything you own cannot be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciple.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, quiconque d’entre vous ne renonce pas à tous ses biens ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.
fr.B: Il en est de même pour vous : celui qui ne se sépare pas de tout ce qu’il possède ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.
fr.R: De la même façon, si l’un de vous ne veut pas laisser derrière lui tout ce qu’il possède, il ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple.

decisions.choice: renounce: say goodbye to, give up one's claim to
decisions.reason: The verb means to say farewell (9:61) and so to part with something. The disciple no longer holds on to what he owns as his own (5:11, 28; 18:22).

decisions.choice: so then: this is the point of the tower and the king
decisions.reason: The builder and the king both count the cost before they start. Following Jesus costs everything, and the hearers must know that before they set out.

decisions.choice: their / they have as the default, his / he has as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Every one of you" includes women and men.

decisions.choice: leave behind
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the verb (m1).

source.text: Καλὸν οὖν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἀρτυθήσεται;

records.literal_gloss: Good therefore the salt; if however even the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?

en.L: Salt, then, [is] good; but if even the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?
en.B: So salt is a good thing. But if even salt goes flat, how will its flavor be brought back?
en.R: Salt is good. But suppose salt stops tasting like salt. There is no way to make it salty again.

fr.L: Le sel, donc, [est] bon ; mais si même le sel devient fade, avec quoi sera-t-il assaisonné ?
fr.B: Le sel est donc une bonne chose. Mais si le sel lui-même perd son goût, comment lui rendre sa saveur ?
fr.R: Le sel, c’est bon. Mais imaginez que le sel n’ait plus le goût du sel. Il n’y a aucun moyen de le rendre salé à nouveau.

decisions.choice: becomes tasteless: loses its saltiness
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to become foolish (Romans 1:22), and here is used of salt that has lost its taste. Some see a play on words: a disciple who turns back is foolish as well as useless.

decisions.choice: salt that loses its taste: salt mixed with other minerals
decisions.reason: Pure salt does not lose its taste, but salt in the ancient world was often gathered with other minerals. When the salt was washed out, what was left looked like salt and was useless.

decisions.choice: with what will it be seasoned: how can the salt itself be made salty again
alternatives: what will season food once the salt has failed
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying that nothing can restore it (compare Mark 9:50). The next sentence says it is thrown out.

decisions.choice: therefore: salt is a picture of the disciple who counts the cost
decisions.reason: The word links the saying to 14:25-33. A disciple who will not pay the price is like salt that has lost its taste.

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m3).

source.text: οὔτε εἰς γῆν οὔτε εἰς κοπρίαν εὔθετόν ἐστιν· ἔξω βάλλουσιν αὐτό.

records.literal_gloss: Neither for soil nor for manure pile fit is it; out they throw it.

en.L: Neither for [the] soil nor for [the] dunghill is it suitable; they throw it outside.
en.B: It is no use for the field, or even for the manure heap; people just throw it away.
en.R: It is not good for the soil, and it is not even good to mix with manure. People throw it out.

fr.L: Il ne convient ni pour la terre ni pour le tas de fumier ; on le jette dehors.
fr.B: Il ne sert à rien, ni pour le champ, ni même pour le tas de fumier ; on le jette, tout simplement.
fr.R: Il n’est pas bon pour la terre, et il n’est même pas bon à mélanger au fumier. Les gens le jettent.

decisions.choice: neither for soil nor for manure: useless for fertilizer
alternatives: salt spread to ruin the land
decisions.reason: Small amounts of salt could be used with manure and on fields. Salt that had lost its taste could not even be used for that.

decisions.choice: the one who has ears to hear, let him hear: everyone able to hear should pay attention and take this to heart
alternatives: a remark about hearing with the ears only
decisions.reason: Jesus ends his hard words with a call to listen, as in 8:8.

decisions.choice: Whoever has ears to hear should listen
